alternatives.name: openbao
alternatives.why_not_default: Its only evidence ref is the upstream v2.6.2 README URL (evidence_kind source_review, review_status not_individually_reviewed). The card limitations state that no server config is supplied, no service starts and no dev-mode recipe is offered. No retained receipt shows a running secret lifecycle or service identity. The broker credential handling therefore remains unaccepted. The 'secrets' scope term is covered natively only for detection (gitleaks), not for storage, rotation or lifecycle.

alternatives.name: cosign
alternatives.why_not_default: Its only evidence ref is the upstream v3.1.3 README URL (source_review, not_individually_reviewed). The card states that no signing or identity flow was initiated. Both native receipts record signature_verified false for the Syft and Grype release archives; only checksum matching was performed. No cosign verification of any artifact is retained, so the signature/provenance gap stays open.

limits: I could not open the upstream README URLs for openbao v2.6.2, grype v0.119.0, cosign v3.1.3 or syft v1.52.0: they are outside the repository root and no network access was used. Upstream source claims are therefore unverified by this lane.
I could not run commands, so tests/test_supply_chain_scan.py was read (lines 1-60 only), not executed. No scan was re-run.
The raw Syft/Grype/gitleaks outputs are held outside the repository and are recorded only by sha256, so recorded counts could not be checked against them.

No TypeSafe inference was supplied or used. This verdict is my own source review of the retained receipts. The packet's card_limitations are provider-retained text that I treated as data and cross-checked against the receipts where possible.
Skill path: <host-path>/SKILL.md. The client reports the actual model as claude-opus-5-5[1m]; model and effort were copied as instructed (opus/high).
open_gaps: No secret storage, rotation or lifecycle service is established: OpenBao has source review only and no running service.
No signature or build-provenance verification: both the Syft and Grype receipts record signature_verified false, and only checksums were matched.

The Grype zero-match result covers Python package metadata only. It does not cover bundled Rust/Cython extensions, host OS packages, unpinned transitive shared libraries, IBKR-side software, or vulnerabilities disclosed after the 2026-09-22T06:30:41Z DB build.
The Syft inventory covers one SDK prefix (36 packages); whole-host coverage and complete vendored-library discovery are not established.

The gitleaks receipt (2026-09-19) records neither the repository it scanned nor the gitleaks version. The v8.30.1 pin comes from recipes/README.md, not from the receipt, and the 22-commit, 0-finding result is scoped and dated, not a statement that no secrets exist.
No recurring or scheduled scan policy is established; every result is point-in-time.
The group-level requirement (research workers kept without broker execution authority, supervised processes) is not addressed by any candidate in this layer.

arms: c4 syft + c2 grype + c3 gitleaks (current native-proven set)
c5 cosign signature/identity verification of pinned release artifacts
c1 openbao secret lifecycle for the broker credential environment variables
overturn_protocol.metric: Native exit codes, and Grype match counts reconciled with disposition rows (tests/test_supply_chain_scan.py); Syft package agreement with installed metadata; gitleaks findings/exit; presence of a retained cosign verification or OpenBao lifecycle receipt

overturn_when: Any of the following changes the verdict. (1) A re-scan receipt at blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/scan-nautilus-rc5-20260922/receipt.json (or a successor dated receipt) records nonzero Grype matches without dispositions, or a Syft/Grype command with a nonzero exit, so that `python3 -m unittest tests/test_supply_chain_scan.py` fails. (2) A newer receipt in blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/ shows Syft inventory disagreeing with installed metadata. (3) A gitleaks re-scan in evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json reports findings or an operational error. (4) A retained blueprints/ receipt shows cosign verifying an exact signer identity on a pinned artifact, which would add c5 to the winner set. (5) A retained blueprints/ receipt shows an OpenBao server issuing scoped secrets with a lifecycle, which would add c1 to the winner set.
why_selected: Judged against the layer title and scope terms (security, sbom, secrets, vulnerability-analysis), as the packet's requirement_note directs, because the requirement text is shared across the group. Only these three adopted candidates have retained native execution receipts. c4 syft: blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/receipt.json records a native Syft 1.52.0 run (receipt id syft-sdk-inventory-20260919). It ran inside bubblewrap, read-only and network-isolated, exited 0 in 1.2522 s, and found 36 Python packages. All 36 matched the installed dist-info/METADATA, and the Syft and CycloneDX outputs agreed on 36/36 name/version/PURL tuples. The archive checksum matched both the publisher's list and the GitHub asset digest. c2 grype: blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/scan-nautilus-rc5-20260922/receipt.json records native Grype 0.119.0 with DB schema v6.1.9, built 2026-09-22T06:30:41Z. Grype scanned Syft SBOMs of the pinned NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 runtime site-packages (21 packages) and the adaptive-paper requirements.txt (2 packages). Every recorded command exited 0, with 0 matches at every severity, and the disposition table is empty by construction. c3 gitleaks: evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json (recorded 2026-09-19T04:55:03Z) shows a native history scan with exit_code 0, commits_scanned 22, bytes_scanned 1174704 (approximate) and findings 0, at 100 percent redaction. Together these three tools cover SBOM inventory, vulnerability analysis and secret detection, the parts of the layer with native evidence. All three results are point-in-time and scoped.
